elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: Rendered 3.4: "Customer may terminate this Agreement (including all Service Option Attachments) or any Service Option Attachment ... for convenience at any time by:" — the Service Option Attachments are the order-level documents referenced in the Order Forms, so both whole-agreement and order-level convenience exits exist. (The deterministic check "Customer convenience termination present: false" is a regex-phrasing artefact; the operative text plainly grants the right.)

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: Operation 1 replaced "at the end of any calendar month" with "at any time" and operation 2 replaced "at least one month's prior written notice" with "at least thirty (30) days' prior written notice", so the effective date is no longer pushed to a month end beyond 30 days.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Inserted at the close of Section 3.4: "IBM will refund to Customer, pro rata, any prepaid charges for the period after the effective date of termination." The words "pro rata" are express (not inferred) and the sentence sits inside the Section 3.4 convenience mechanic.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: Already met on the retained text: IBM's only mid-term exit is 3.3 material breach ("Customer or IBM may terminate this Agreement for material breach ... upon written notice"), and 3.2 is a 90-day non-renewal notice expressly operating "prior to the end of the then-current term", i.e. natural-term non-renewal assessed under RENEWAL, not mid-term T4C. No Vendor convenience right exists during the committed term.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Section 3.4(a) as amended requires "at least thirty (30) days' prior written notice", so a 60- to 90-day notice is permitted a fortiori; the right is exercisable "at any time", not only at a month end.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: Section 3.4(b) is retained unchanged: "paying the applicable early termination charges, if any, specified in Attachment A and applicable Service Option Attachments." No cap is inserted in operative language; the three-months cap is only promised in the rationale as a negotiating fallback. To reach the fallback level the drafter must add words such as "provided that such early termination charges will not exceed three (3) months' charges for the terminated Services".

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: Condition does not bite adversely: IBM has no convenience right at all. Its only non-breach exit is the 3.2 election given "at least ninety (90) days prior to the end of the then-current term", which terminates the Service Option Attachment at term end (non-renewal), so IBM cannot exit mid-term for convenience.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Vacuously satisfied plus supported by text: IBM has no convenience right, and its only elective exit (3.2 non-renewal) already requires ninety (90) days' written notice.

reasons: Position-complete at the preferred level: all four preferred elements are met on the rendered operative language (at-any-time exercise, 30-day notice, express pro-rata refund of prepaid charges, and no Vendor mid-term convenience right).

Fallback is incomplete solely because Section 3.4(b) retains uncapped "early termination charges, if any". That does not block the finding (preferred is complete), but if the fallback is ever taken the drafter must insert an express operative cap of three (3) months' charges rather than relying on the comment.

Minimality holds: three surgical operations, each traceable to a preferred element (month-end restriction removed and notice reset for the 30-day element; refund sentence added for the refund element). Favourable retained language is untouched — the prerequisite Service Option Attachment carve-out, "if any" in 3.4(b), 3.4's continuing-performance sentence, and 3.3's bar on IBM recovering 3.4(b) charges after its own breach. No survival tail, expense language, procedure or other model-language extras were bolted on.

Intent preserved: the cross-reference in 3.3 to "the early termination charges described in Section 3.4(b)" still resolves because 3.4(b) is retained verbatim; the 3.2 renewal/non-renewal mechanic is untouched and is correctly routed to RENEWAL rather than double-flagged here; no undefined term or contradictory retained sentence results ("at any time" and "at least thirty (30) days' prior written notice" operate consistently).

Deviation status is correct: the original clause failed the fallback on a material term (uncapped early termination charges, plus a month-end effective date that could exceed the notice period with no refund of prepaid charges), so a redline was warranted.

One drafting nit worth flagging to the client but not a defect: the inserted refund sentence would read more tightly if expressly anchored ("In the event of a termination under this Section 3.4, IBM will refund ...") to foreclose any argument that it is a free-standing sentence outside the convenience mechanic.
